papers.title_en: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models
papers.authors: Junyi Wu, Zekun Li, Chenhongyi Yang, Chen Guo, Lingchen Yang, Yongan Zhang, Xinyi Zhang, Hongbing Hu, Bartek Rymkowski, Srinath Sridhar, Yan Yan, Xijie Huang
papers.evidence: 带持久记忆的相机可控视频世界模型
papers.tldr: 视频世界模型在长时程生成中会出现空间记忆衰减，超出当前上下文后难以保持场景一致。World-T3 将测试时训练作为持久记忆，用递归最小二乘规则按相机位姿在线更新快权重参数，把历史观测写入模型参数，再通过双教师分布匹配蒸馏为少步生成器。在长时程重访基准上，重访 PSNR 由 13.52 提升至 18.31 dB，绝对旋转误差从 3.344 降至 1.075。该方法以恒定存储和单步计算实现实时交互生成，在单张 B200 上以 1280×704 达到 20.6 FPS。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in video world models have enabled plausible interactive environments, yet long-horizon generation places a fundamental demand on visual memory: the previously observed world must remain consistent as the model continues to generate. Existing autoregressive approaches often implicitly rely on the generative model itself to retain such information, leading to spatial memory decay beyond the active context. We introduce World-T3, a camera-controlled video world model with a test-time training memory that consolidates past observations into dedicated model parameters. To robustly update this memory, we propose a recursive least-squares rule that incrementally absorbs novel visual features via online pose-keyed memory updates. Our TTT memory reads out previously observed scene features from the fast-weight state by camera pose, enabling consistent generation with constant storage and per-step computation regardless of rollout length. To facilitate real-time interactive generation with this robust memory, we further distill the autoregressive model into a few-step generator via dual-teacher distribution matching. On a long-horizon revisit benchmark, World-T3 raises revisit PSNR from 13.52 to 18.31 dB and reduces absolute rotation error from 3.344 to 1.075 relative to the strongest baseline on both metrics, while sustaining 20.6 FPS at 1280 x 704 on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.

papers.title_en: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
papers.authors: Hongchang Liu, Jian Liu, Yujuan Ding, Liang Peng, Xun Jiang, Fei Ma, Xing Xu, Yi Bin
papers.evidence: 用于预测式三维世界建模的视角解耦几何状态
papers.tldr: 现有3D世界模型常以几何基础模型特征作为预测世界状态，但视角依赖会把场景动态与相机变化纠缠，使状态演化更难预测。GeoState提出视角解耦的几何状态表示：场景tokenizer聚合多视角特征形成场景状态，几何解码器再用相机射线查询。自回归世界模型单独预测未来场景状态与相机运动，因此可在预测或外部指定相机下解码，并保持单一上下文尺度。在Waymo上优于已有方法，支持跨视角一致查询，并零样本泛化到KITTI和nuScenes。
papers.abstract_en: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/

papers.title_en: Momentum: Persistent Dynamics for Video World Models
papers.authors: Nedko Savov, Stefan Maria Ailuro, Danda Pani Paudel, Yilun Du, Xi Wang, Luc Van Gool
papers.evidence: 视频世界模型视野外的持久动态
papers.tldr: 现有视频世界模型依赖历史观测、静态点云或图像缓存，难以更新视野外动态内容，导致物体离开后遗忘或错误重现。Momentum 用八相机参考装置同步视频表示演化场景，并在装置图上传播生成以协调时空动态。其两阶段流程 WorldUpdate 构建共享动态记忆，WorldInteract 以该记忆约束目标相机视频生成。实验在未见街景中把动态一致性较静态图像条件提升 126.2%，并改善视觉保真度。
papers.abstract_en: Video world models must capture how a scene evolves beyond the current camera view to generate consistent observations when its content reappears. Existing approaches rely on observation history, static point clouds, or image caches constructed from past frames. These representations are often expensive and, more importantly, cannot update dynamic scene content outside the field of view: generated vehicles and pedestrians may be forgotten after leaving the field of view or reappear in physically inaccurate states. We represent an evolving scene through synchronized videos from reference-camera rigs, each comprising eight cameras that jointly cover the surrounding scene. We connect these rigs in a graph and propagate video generation between neighboring rigs to coordinate scene dynamics across locations and time. We introduce Momentum, a two-stage pipeline: WorldUpdate jointly generates reference-camera videos as a shared memory of scene dynamics, and WorldInteract grounds camera-controlled video generation in this evolving memory, allowing moving content to remain represented outside the target view and reappear consistently. To support training and evaluation, we develop a CARLA pipeline that captures synchronized videos from reference camera rigs and a moving target camera, together with an evaluation framework measuring consistency within the generated world state and the target observations.Experiments on generated street scenes show that grounding target videos in scene dynamics generated by Momentum improves dynamic scene consistency by 126.2% in unseen scenes over static image conditioning, while also improving visual fidelity. Our models and source code will be made publicly available.

papers.title_en: Gen Through the Lens: Camera-Controllable Video Generation via Cross-Coordinate Conditioning Fusion
papers.authors: Shuai Li, Jinxu Xiang, Xinyuan Li, Hanlei Guo, Xiyang Tan, Alan Zhao, Xiaotong Zhao, Ran Zhang
papers.evidence: 结合空间几何提示的相机可控视频生成
papers.tldr: 现有相机可控视频生成多将相机运动视为抽象条件或依赖单一坐标系，难以兼顾真实感与物理一致性。本文提出Gen Through the Lens，将控制信号分解到相机、世界与物体三个坐标空间，并通过跨坐标条件融合统一引导生成。实验表明，该方法在多种相机操作下实现可控且视觉一致的结果，在真实感与可编辑性上优于现有方法，为精细相机控制提供新方案。
papers.abstract_en: We present Gen Through the Lens, a camera-controllable image-to-video generation framework that synthesizes videos from a given reference image while enabling realistic and physically consistent camera operations. Unlike previous models that treat camera motion as abstract conditioning or rely on a single coordinate system, our approach explicitly decomposes and fuses control signals across three coordinate spaces: the camera coordinate (modeled by intrinsic parameters), the world coordinate (represented by spatial geometry hints), and the object coordinate (described by 3D bounding boxes of target subjects). Through cross-coordinate conditioning fusion, these heterogeneous cues are unified to guide the generative process, enabling precise control of camera motion, focus, and framing while preserving temporal and spatial coherence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method produces controllable and visually consistent results across diverse camera operations, outperforming existing approaches in both realism and editability.

papers.title_en: Generative World Simulation with DAO and JING
papers.authors: XGEN Team, Guohao Cai, Haoxuan Che, Frank Fan, Chenran Huang, Junjia Huang, Jiayi Jiang, Yanheng Li, Leon Liu, Shaoteng Liu, Xi Liu, Feng Nie, Zhefan Rao, An Wang, Hanwen Wang, Pengxiang Yan, Jieming Yu, Qian Zha, Wentao Zheng
papers.evidence: 持久共享世界状态与可控动态及第一人称视听生成
papers.tldr: 现有交互世界难以同时保持持久共享状态与连续第一人称视听体验。本文提出生成式世界模拟框架，将可计算世界引擎DAO与自我中心交互体验模型JING耦合。DAO维护角色、物体、空间及关系并按规则和世界时间演化，JING依据观察者条件、历史与动作生成视听体验。框架支持人类与智能体持续探索、操作和交流，使世界保留历史并随行动演化。
papers.abstract_en: We present a Generative World Simulation framework that couples persistent shared world state with continuous first-person audiovisual generation. The framework integrates DAO, a computable world engine, and JING, an Egocentric Interactive Experience Model, to support sustained interaction for humans and agents. DAO maintains the states of characters, objects, and spaces and their relationships, advancing the world according to interaction rules and world time while preserving the consequences of past actions. From this evolving state, DAO derives observer-specific conditions for JING, which combines these conditions with character, object, and scene references, observation history, and current actions to generate each observer's audiovisual experience. Users can explore environments, manipulate objects, and communicate with characters through viewpoint control and text instructions, with their actions shaping both the shared state and subsequent experiences. By connecting world-state evolution with experience generation in a continuous interaction loop, the framework offers an approach to building interactive worlds that retain their history, evolve through action, and persist beyond any individual observer.

papers.title_en: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
papers.authors: Dongyue Lu, Guian Fang, Hur Lim, Yonggang Wu, Yanrong Wang, Hongshan Chen, Shengju Qian, Yue Liao, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Tianxin Huang, Yu Yang, Hongji Yang, Junchao Huang, Ao Liang, Yihao Wang, Zihan Wang, Rong Li, Hanlin Chen, Xin Wang, Wei Tsang Ooi, Mike Zheng Shou, Shuicheng Yan
papers.evidence: 交互式世界模型三维一致性基准
papers.tldr: 视频生成器常被当作可交互世界，但画面逼真不代表具备一致的3D结构。Orbia构建首个系统评估交互式世界模型3D一致性的基准，围绕输入保持、生成内容持久性和3D自一致性设计探索与回访协议。它汇集720个室内外实例和六种协议，评测27个文本、动作与相机条件模型。该基准能定位长期3D不一致，为更持久的世界模型提供诊断依据。
papers.abstract_en: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. For generated-content persistence, we compare revisits to regions absent from the input image with their first generated observations to test whether models preserve what they create. For 3D self-consistency, cross-view depth and feature correspondence, regional scale agreement, and held-out Gaussian rendering test whether generated views describe the same 3D scene. Minute-long exploration and revisits further test long-term consistency. Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.
